title: Perfect Setup
transcript: White's brilliant idea is rook to c3 with a check because despite being up a knight and a pawn, it is going to be extremely [music] hard to convert this position into a win. But after king to d6, black is creating a threat on one of our own pieces. And now moving the rook away wouldn't get us any closer to achieving our goal. So we have to become creative and play the brilliant rook to c4 leaving this rook to hang. Realizing that if black takes, actually after we capture back this rook, the advantage of having a pawn left is going to become more crushing once black is only left with one rook. And if black takes the other rook like this, now after knight takes c4 with a check, we are forking the king and rook. So we would end up in this other ending which is still winning. But wait a second because white is not out of the woods quite yet. After rook to c4, black has rook takes b4 and this takes away the last hope of converting the win for white. That pawn was essential to get a new queen and the two rooks are defending each other with an x-ray through the white rook while this other rook is still hanging. So is this it? Is white actually losing in this position? Well, not exactly. White has the majestic rook seven to e4 and the geometry of this position works out perfectly for white. There is no defensive x-ray. But this is also technically a double attack. This white rook is attacking this rook and this white rook is attacking this black rook. So you cannot move away without losing one of the two. And unfortunately for black, capturing either rook is going to allow a recapture with the white knight with a check. And although the black king can fork the knight and rook, after [music] rook takes f4, we maintain a rook and we also defend the knight. And we are going to win this game.
